title: Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Materials (Liquid Glass)
lede: The HIG page that defines where Liquid Glass belongs: a functional layer for controls and navigation that floats above an opaque content layer.
summary: Apple’s rules for Liquid Glass: controls only, regular and clear variants, and a dimming layer.
made: 2025 (Liquid Glass section added with the June 2025 update; text read in October 2026)

evidence.note: Read the page text through its JSON data endpoint (developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/design/human-interface-guidelines/materials.json) on 2026-10-02, because the HTML page renders with JavaScript. The page’s example images were not inspected.

styles.note: The primary written source for the style’s rules: glass only on the control layer, two variants, and legibility measures.

context: “Liquid Glass forms a distinct functional layer for controls and navigation elements — like tab bars and sidebars — that floats above the content layer.” Content can “scroll and peek through from beneath these elements”.

“Don’t use Liquid Glass in the content layer.” The exception is transient controls such as sliders and toggles, which take on the glass look while a person uses them. “Use Liquid Glass effects sparingly.”

The regular variant “blurs and adjusts the luminosity of background content”. The clear variant “is highly translucent” and is for components over photos and videos. Over bright content, “consider adding a dark dimming layer of 35% opacity”.

Standard materials (blur, vibrancy, and blending modes) stay in use for structure in the content layer, beneath the glass. All quotes: [Apple HIG: Materials](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/materials).
interpretation: The rule that glass belongs only to controls is what separates the style from glassmorphism, where glass cards carry the content.
borrow: Choose the glass variant by what sits behind it: regular over text and mixed content, clear only over media, with a dimming layer when the media is bright.

rights.statement: Apple documentation; copyrighted. Quoted briefly. No image is stored here.
